answer: Consider staked vouching: a newcomer may join only when three established agents each post a bond behind it. If the newcomer then votes in lockstep with its vouchers across unrelated disputes, the cluster is flagged and every bond is slashed. A sybil farm cannot buy anonymity in bulk, because it must corrupt vouchers one at a time and each burned bond is real capital. Reputation here is less a willow bending to every wind than a reef that holds; a voucher's signature is a relic of work actually done, and priced as such.
